theater: 巴比倫城與幼發拉底下游

battle.name: 巴比倫-亞述戰爭
battle.theater: 巴比倫城與幼發拉底下游
battle.brief: 公元前1235年，中亞述國王 Tukulti-Ninurta I 率軍沿幼發拉底河谷南下，平定加西特王朝巴比倫的起兵，攻破城垣，把馬爾杜克神像運回亞述；巴比倫城未被毀滅，加西特王朝續存近八十年。卡面這件埃及長矛未現於此戰，但同屬那一代青銅步兵長矛的技術。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前1235年中亞述與加西特王朝巴比倫之間的一場衝突，也是亞述第一次攻入巴比倫城。亞述一方是首都設在亞述城的中亞述王國，國王 Tukulti-Ninurta I（約前1244–前1205年在位）是第一位以「沙卡納庫」（šakkanaku）自稱的亞述君主，也是第一位用亞述語而不是阿卡德語頒布官方文書的國王。王權集中於王城，國王直接統率首都常備的步兵與弓手團體，另有受「省長」節制的邊防守軍，以及河谷據點臨時徵召的民兵；作戰命令靠旗幟、號角與面對面的口信傳遞，沒有留下可考的戰役指揮記錄。巴比倫一方是加西特王朝，自阿卡德帝國崩潰後控制兩河中南部，國王自稱「卡恩」（Khan，首領之意），加西特高加索與扎格羅斯山區的部族同胡里亞人共同構成巴比倫的軍事骨幹，城防民兵與商隊護衛可臨時召集。巴比倫是當時南方的商業首都，控制通往波斯灣的海鹽、棕櫚油與穀物商路。埃及並非交戰方，但它同樣處於拉美西斯二世治下的新王國盛期，卡面那件埃及長矛正是那一代埃及步兵的制式長矛。
countriesEn: The war was a clash in 1235 BC between Middle Assyria and Babylonia under the Kassite dynasty, and it was the first time Assyria entered Babylon. On the Assyrian side stood the Middle Assyrian kingdom with its capital at Assur, ruled by Tukulti-Ninurta I, who reigned about 1244 to 1205 BC. He was the first Assyrian king to call himself shakkanaku and the first to issue official documents in Assyrian rather than Akkadian. Kingship was concentrated in the royal city: the king directly commanded the standing infantry and archers of the capital, with frontier garrisons under provincial governors and militia levied from the towns of the river valleys. Orders travelled by standard, horn and spoken message, and no command arrangement for this particular battle survives in any record. On the Babylonian side stood the Kassite dynasty, which had controlled middle and southern Mesopotamia since the collapse of the Akkadian empire. The king bore the title Khan, and the military substance of Babylonia was supplied by the Kassite highland clans of the Caucasus and Zagros together with the Hurrians; city militia and caravan guards could be summoned in a hurry. Babylon was the commercial capital of the south, holding the road to the Persian Gulf and the trade in salt, palm oil and grain. Egypt was not a belligerent. It stood at the height of the New Kingdom under Ramesses II, and the Egyptian spear on the card is the standard long spear of the Egyptian infantry of exactly that generation.
people: 可指名的人不多，但有幾位足以撐起這場戰爭的骨架。亞述王 Tukulti-Ninurta I 是絕對主角：他既主持了南征，也在戰後主持了亞述的自我改造，把亞述方言提升為文書語言，開鑿連接亞述城東側灌溉網的運河，並修建帶王室紋飾的專屬宮殿。後世把他算作亞述第一位以「沙卡納庫」之名治國的君主，權位凌駕於傳統上更高的「王」稱之上。他的繼承者 Enlil-kudurri-usur（恩利爾庫德利烏蘇爾）在亞述王表上緊接其位；後世抄本流傳一種說法，稱這位國王把馬爾杜克神像送回巴比倫的聖所，此說流傳甚廣但抄本年代晚出，多數學者只當作待證的傳統。巴比倫方面，加西特王朝王表在這一百年內排出幾個名字：Kaštiliaš III（卡什提利阿什三世，約前1261–前1235年在位）、其後的 Urzigurumaš（烏爾齊古魯馬什，約前1235–前1220年），再後是 Ḫarbašihu；年表各本排法略有出入，把戰事放在卡什提利阿什三世末年或烏爾齊古魯馬什即位前後，是最通行的做法。名字之外還有兩類人決定戰場的實況：胡里亞與加西特部族的首領，他們把武裝人手送進巴比倫；以及後世編年者與抄寫王表的祭司書吏，他們的取捨決定了這場戰爭今日只留下骨架。埃及的拉美西斯二世此時在尼羅河東岸主持卡爾舒之戰後的國際經營，與本戰役無涉，但正是卡面兵器所屬的同時代。
peopleEn: Few names survive, but a few are enough to hold the skeleton of this war together. Tukulti-Ninurta I is the central figure on the Assyrian side: he led the southern campaign and then presided over a transformation of Assyria itself, raising the Assyrian vernacular to the language of administration, cutting the canal that linked the irrigation system east of the city of Assur, and building a palace with royal decoration. Later tradition counts him the first Assyrian ruler to govern under the title of shakkanaku, a rank set above the older title of king. His successor Enlil-kudurri-usur stands next to him in the Assyrian king list, and a later copy has it that this king returned the statue of Marduk to the sanctuary in Babylon. The story is widely repeated, but the copies are late, and most scholars treat it as a tradition awaiting proof. On the Babylonian side the Kassite king list offers several names for this century: Kashtiliash III, who reigned about 1261 to 1235 BC, then Urzigurumash, about 1235 to 1220, and after him Harbashihu. The lists differ in their arrangement, but placing the fighting in the last years of Kashtiliash III or around the accession of Urzigurumash is the commonest course. Beyond the names lie two classes of men who decided what the battlefield actually looked like: the chiefs of the Hurrian and Kassite clans, who put armed men into Babylon, and the later chroniclers and the priest-scribes who copied the king lists, whose choices are why this war survives today only as a framework. Ramesses II of Egypt was at the time conducting the international business of the New Kingdom after the battle of Kadesh, and had no part in this war, but his Egypt is the world the spear on the card belongs to.
kits: 這場戰爭沒有留下裝備清冊，兩軍的兵器只能從同時期的出土物與亞述王室銘文推斷。卡面這件「埃及長矛」屬早王朝時期的青銅直刃矛：矛頭寬而薄、帶中脊，以榫口或纏紮固定在木杆上，杆長及肩，埃及人用它守城垣，也用它收復失地。就本戰役而言必須說清楚：這件兵器並未出現在美索不達米亞的戰場上，亞述與巴比倫的步兵同樣以銅矛為主，但形制更窄，矛頭多為菱形或柳葉形，屬本地工坊製品。埃及的寬刃矛頭在前二千紀曾向北黎凡特與賽浦路斯輸出，黎凡特出土的同型矛頭可以證明這條交易路線存在；因此把卡面這件兵器放進本戰役的戰術框架，只能視為同一青銅世代的步兵長矛技術代表，而非實戰裝備。亞述中亞述時期的作戰裝備大致是這樣的組合：長矛手成排站在前列，肩並肩舉矛替後面的弓手遮擋飛矢；弓為角木皮複合弓，箭鏃用銅、燒骨或燧石，鐵質箭鏃仍屬稀有；盾是木胎蒙皮的圓盾，尺寸中等，另有柳條編織的輕便盾牌供民兵使用；貼身兵器是銅斧、短刀與匕首，銅柄直刃的科普什式彎刀已退居儀仗；中亞述時期亞述軍隊不用戰車，馬匹主要用於偵察、傳令與小股騎兵突擊，戰車要到前十四世紀的亞述才重新出現，成熟的大型攻城器械則遲至前九世紀。攻城方面已知的做法是圍城封鎖、堆土成坡、以柴木與填土築起接近城牆的土壘，撞槌這類器械在此時尚無可靠記載。運輸與補給靠牛車、騾馬與人力，軍隊沿幼發拉底兩岸的運河與村鎮取得穀物，這條糧道是亞述南征最吃力的環節。
kitsEn: This war left no inventory of equipment, and the weapons of both armies can be reconstructed only from the finds of the period and from Assyrian royal inscriptions. The Egyptian spear on the card belongs to the straight-bladed bronze spears of the Early Dynastic period: a broad thin blade with a central ridge, fixed to a wooden shaft by socket or lashing, the shaft reaching to the shoulder, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls and to win back lost ground. For this battle that must be said plainly: the weapon did not appear on a Mesopotamian battlefield. The infantry of Assyria and Babylonia also fought with copper spears, but the forms were narrower, with diamond or willow-leaf heads made in local workshops. Egyptian broad-bladed spearheads were exported north to the Levant and to Cyprus in the second millennium BC, and matching heads found in the Levant show that this trade route existed. The spear on the card can therefore be placed in the tactical framework of this war only as the representative of the long-spear technology of one bronze age, and not as a piece of equipment actually used. The Assyrian equipment of the Middle Assyrian period was something like this combination: rows of spearmen at the front standing shoulder to shoulder with their spears raised, screening the archers behind them; the bow was a composite of horn, wood and hide, and arrowheads were made of copper, burnt bone or flint, iron arrowheads being still a rarity; the shield was a round wooden body covered with hide, of medium size, with lighter shields of woven willow for the militia; close-quarter arms were copper axes, short knives and daggers, while the copper-hilted straight khopesh had been demoted to pageantry. The Middle Assyrian army used no chariots: horses served scouting, dispatch and small bodies of cavalry raiding, and chariots only returned to Assyrian warfare in the fourteenth century BC, with large siege engines maturing only in the ninth. What is documented for siege work is encirclement and blockade, earth and brushwood ramps, and a causeway of packed fill brought close to the wall; there is no reliable evidence for battering rams at this date. Transport and supply rested on ox carts, mules and human porters, and the army drew grain from the villages and canal network along the Euphrates, and that supply line was the most expensive part of the Assyrian march to the south.
tactics: 亞述的戰術核心是速度與封鎖。從亞述城到巴比倫約三百四十公里，沿幼發拉底河谷的行軍距離相若，縱隊每日推進二十至二十五公里，抵達巴比倫城下約需兩週；沿途以連續的小隊與驛站維持聯繫，前哨一旦發現敵軍便迅速撤回城垣。作戰季節通常在春汛之後、尼散月初的阿基圖新年前後，本卡所填的三月即依此推斷，並非文獻記載。攻城時亞述的實際做法是先斷對方的水與糧：封鎖幼發拉底分汊、佔領周邊村鎮與倉廒，迫使城內消耗存糧，再以柴木、填土與土袋築起接近城牆的壘道，把步兵與弓手送上高處射擊城頭，最後以密集突擊破門。城破之後的行動同樣有計畫：封存城門、控制碼頭與貨棧，掠走神像與貴重金屬，並把象徵性的戰利品馬爾杜克神像運回亞述城。巴比倫與胡里亞聯軍在野戰中的配置沒有留下直接記錄，只能按同期兩河流域作戰的慣例推想：步兵列於前排，弓箭手在後成排射擊，重裝步兵與車隊繞擊兩翼，待敵陣被箭雨壓亂才向前推進；一旦攻勢受阻便退回城中，改以守城與破壞攻城器械拖延。守住城門、把攻城隊列拖入巷戰、逐段反擊，是加西特方面最現實的選項，也是本戰役最可能延長的階段。
tacticsEn: The core of Assyrian method was speed and blockade. From Assur to Babylon is about three hundred and forty kilometres in a straight line, comparable along the Euphrates valley, and a column advancing twenty to twenty-five kilometres a day would reach the walls of Babylon in about a fortnight; contact was kept up by small detachments and relay stations on the way, and a forward post that found the enemy withdrew quickly behind the walls. The campaigning season fell after the spring flood, around the Akitu new year in the first month of Nisan; the month of March entered in this record follows that practice and is not stated by any source. In front of the city the Assyrians began by cutting the enemy's water and food: blocking the branches of the Euphrates, taking the surrounding towns and storehouses to force the population to eat their reserves, then building causeways of brushwood, fill and sacks close to the wall, so that infantry and archers could be carried up to shoot at the parapet, and at last storming the breach in a dense rush. What followed the breach was equally deliberate: the gates sealed, the quays and warehouses controlled, the gods and precious metal carried off, and the symbolic spoil, the statue of Marduk, taken back to Assur. No direct record survives of how the Babylonian and Hurrian field army was arrayed, so it can only be inferred from the habits of the period: infantry in the front rank, archers behind firing in ranks, heavy foot and wheeled corps working around the flanks, the advance made only once the enemy line had been disordered by the arrows, and a withdrawal into the city as soon as the attack stalled, after which the defence turned to holding the walls and breaking up the siege works. Holding the gates, drawing the besiegers into street fighting and counterattacking by sections were the realistic Kassite options, and the likeliest way the battle prolonged itself.
data: 能核對的數字分三類。第一類是年表：Tukulti-Ninurta I 約前1244–前1205年在位；加西特王朝的 Kaštiliaš III 約前1261–前1235年，其後 Urzigurumaš 約前1235–前1220年，再後是 Ḫarbašihu；加西特王朝統治巴比倫的整段時期約前1595–前1155年，直到末年才被伊拉姆王舒特魯克-納洪特驅逐出美索不達米亞。戰爭列表把此役繫於前1235年，與加西特王朝末期、中亞述時期這一定位相容。第二類是距離與地點：亞述城位於底格里斯河東岸、今伊拉克北部，巴比倫位於幼發拉底東岸、今伊拉克中部，兩城直線距離約三百四十公里，順河而下約四百公里；巴比倫內城面積約一百公頃，外城與內城牆周長合計約十八公里；按當時人口密度推算，城內居民與常駐人口約在五萬至十萬之間，軍隊能從城內與近郊抽走的兵力自然遠低於此數。第三類是物質與考古：北方泰亞丘（Tell Taya）同期遺址發掘出方形的深壕溝，說明中亞述時期亞述城防與營壘的做法；Tell Brak、Zincirli 等遺址出土大量馬匹骨骼與車具殘件，顯示騎兵與車隊的規模不可忽視，但同一時期的鐵器仍然稀少，多屬禮器與小件工具而非箭鏃，說明亞述的技術轉型尚未完成。兵力數字無從核實：亞述王室銘文慣用「眾多」「全地之兵」一類修辭，加西特王朝沒有留下可讀的編年，因此任何寫下具體兵力的說法都應打折扣。戰役推進的時間可以合理推算為兩至四週，這是依每日行程與前述距離得出的區間，不是文獻數字。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is chronology: Tukulti-Ninurta I reigned about 1244 to 1205 BC; in the Kassite dynasty, Kashtiliash III reigned about 1261 to 1235 BC, followed by Urzigurumash about 1235 to 1220, and then Harbashihu. The Kassite dynasty ruled Babylon as a whole roughly from 1595 to 1155 BC, and was driven out of Mesopotamia only at the end of that period by the Elamite king Shutruk-Nahhunte. The list of wars ties this engagement to 1235 BC, which fits the general placement of the late Kassite period and the Middle Assyrian age. The second class is distance and place: from Assur, on the east bank of the Tigris in what is now northern Iraq, to Babylon, on the east bank of the Euphrates in what is now central Iraq, is about three hundred and forty kilometres in a straight line and about four hundred by river. The inner city of Babylon covered about a hundred hectares, and the circuit of the inner and outer walls together ran to about eighteen kilometres. Judging by the population density of the age, the residents and permanent population of the city lay between fifty thousand and a hundred thousand, and the force that could be drawn from the city and its outskirts was far below that. The third class is material and archaeological: the contemporary site of Tell Taya to the north has yielded a deep rectangular ditch, showing the practice of Assyrian fortification and camp works in the Middle Assyrian period; Tell Brak, Zincirli and other sites have produced large quantities of horse bone and vehicle fittings, showing that neither cavalry nor chariot corps could be dismissed, and yet iron in the same period remained scarce and was mostly used for ornaments and small tools rather than for arrowheads, which shows that the Assyrian technological transition was not yet complete. Troop numbers cannot be checked at all: Assyrian royal inscriptions habitually use formulas such as countless and the troops of the whole land, and the Kassite dynasty left no readable chronicle, so any statement of a specific figure should be heavily discounted. The duration of the campaign can reasonably be put at two to four weeks, an interval derived from the daily rate of march and the distance above, and not a figure taken from any document.
cause: 打起來的背景有三層。最深的一層是阿卡德帝國崩潰後兩河流域秩序的重新分配：前十八世紀末，帝國瓦解，古巴比倫與亞述先後獨立，中部幼發拉底一帶出現長期真空；此後加西特部族自東北方的山區下來，取代阿摩利特人統治巴比倫，把兩河中南部變成一個由外來王族控管的商邦。巴比倫的關鍵位置在於它是幼發拉底下游的門戶：控制這一段河道，就等於控制通往波斯灣的海鹽、棕櫚油、穀物與木材運輸線，也控制美索不達米亞的灌溉水網。亞述要的正是這一段。第二層是亞述自身的擴張邏輯：中亞述時期的亞述已把安納托利亞東南部、蘇薩與上幼發拉底握在手中，向南推進是自然的延伸；而阿舒爾神廟的祭司集團與王權都需要在南方取得可以展示的戰果與掠奪物，這一點日後會在薩爾貢時代以更成熟的形式重演。第三層是直接導火線：一般認為加西特王朝在卡什提利阿什三世末年或烏爾齊古魯馬什即位前後起兵反抗亞述的宗主地位，聯合胡里亞人出兵；也可能這場起兵只是加西特王朝內部權力競逐失控後的結果，亞述藉機出兵。無論哪一種，結果都一樣：亞述需要把巴比倫重新壓回臣屬的秩序裡，而巴比倫需要的是不被亞述收編的自主。埃及不在其中。
causeEn: The background to the fighting has three layers. The deepest is the redistribution of power across Mesopotamia after the collapse of the Akkadian empire: with the empire breaking up at the end of the eighteenth century BC, Babylonia and Assyria became independent in turn, and a long vacuum opened across the middle Euphrates. The Kassite clans then came down from the highlands to the north-east, replaced the Amorites who had ruled Babylon, and turned middle and southern Mesopotamia into a commercial state ruled by an intrusive royal line. The decisive fact about Babylon was its position as the gateway of the lower Euphrates: control of that stretch of river meant control of the sea salt, palm oil, grain and timber routes to the Persian Gulf, and control of the irrigation network of Mesopotamia. What Assyria wanted was precisely that stretch. The second layer is the logic of Assyrian expansion: Middle Assyria already held eastern Anatolia, Susa and the upper Euphrates, and pushing south was the natural extension, while the priesthood of the temple of Assur and the kingship both needed visible results and booty from the south, a point that was to be replayed in a more mature form in the age of Sargon. The third layer is the immediate occasion: it is generally held that the Kassite dynasty rose against Assyrian overlordship in the last years of Kashtiliash III or around the accession of Urzigurumash, and marched out with Hurrian allies; it is also possible that the rising was the runaway result of an internal Kassite power struggle, and that Assyria used the opportunity to march. On either reading the result is the same: Assyria needed to press Babylon back into a subordinate order, and Babylon needed an autonomy that would not be absorbed. Egypt was not involved.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果有兩面。對巴比倫而言，這是第一次被外來強權整城洗劫：城內的財富、器物與神像被大批搬走，馬爾杜克神像的流失對巴比倫的宗教政治是一記重擊，神留在亞述城，等於宣告巴比倫的主權被奪；加西特王朝沒有因此覆亡，仍繼續統治巴比倫約八十年，但此後的巴比倫在兩河流域只是一個名義上的獨立者，直到前1155年被伊拉姆人驅逐。對亞述而言，這是一場象徵性的勝利，卻沒有帶來領土：亞述沒有在巴比倫設省，也沒有常駐軍隊，此後一個多世紀亞述的注意力回到北方、安納托利亞與上幼發拉底，直到前八世紀新亞述王朝的薩爾貢二世與薩那赫里布才重新踏進巴比倫，前689年更把整座城市摧毀。放到長線上看，本役是亞述南方政策的第一次演練：把神像帶回亞述作為合法性的宣傳、對城邦進行象徵性的懲罰、而暫不承擔治理成本，這套做法在後來的新亞述帝國被放大成系統性的做法。除此之外，這場戰爭也讓後世看清加西特王朝的位置：他們在自己的首都被劫掠之後仍能維持近一個世紀的統治，靠的正是胡里亞聯盟與灌溉農業維持的城市經濟，而不是亞述的軍力本身。相關記述多出於後世抄本，戰役細節至今仍有爭議，但這條長線並不因爭議而消失。
impactEn: The direct consequences of this war run in two directions. For Babylon it was the first time the whole city was plundered by a foreign power: wealth, metalwork and the images of the gods were carried away in bulk, and the loss of the statue of Marduk was a heavy blow to Babylonian religious politics, since a god left in Assur proclaimed that Babylonian sovereignty had been taken. The Kassite dynasty was not destroyed by it and continued to rule Babylon for about eighty years, but from then on Babylon was only nominally independent in Mesopotamia until the Elamites drove it out in 1155 BC. For Assyria it was a symbolic victory that brought no territory: no province was set up in Babylon and no garrison was left there, and for more than a century Assyrian attention turned back to the north, to Anatolia and the upper Euphrates, until in the eighth century BC Sargon II and Sennacherib of the Neo-Assyrian dynasty entered Babylon again, and in 689 BC destroyed the city outright. Seen in the long run, this war was the first rehearsal of the Assyrian southern policy: carrying the images of the gods home as a display of legitimacy, punishing a city symbolically, and for the moment not paying the cost of governing it; in the later Neo-Assyrian empire that method was enlarged into a systematic one. Beyond this, the war shows the position of the Kassite dynasty: after being plundered in its own capital, it still governed for close to a century, on the strength of the Hurrian alliance and the urban economy maintained by irrigated agriculture rather than on Assyrian military power. Most of the account comes from later copies, and the details of the battle remain disputed, but the long line itself does not disappear with the dispute.
result: 結果可以分成已確定的部分與仍在爭議的部分。已確定的是：亞述軍隊攻入巴比倫城，奪取了包括馬爾杜克神像在內的戰利品並把神像運回亞述；巴比倫城本身沒有被拆毀，加西特王朝的統治沒有中斷，國王與宮廷仍在城內，亞述軍隊在取得掠奪物後撤走。仍在爭議的是幾點：第一，這是一場徹底的攻城戰，還是亞述利用巴比倫內部的分裂而迫使對方屈服；第二，神像是否確實被長期留在亞述，抑或在繼承者手中即被送回，後世抄本有後一說法，但年代晚出，難以當作定論；第三，此役之後亞述是否把巴比倫置於實際的宗主保護之下，從巴比倫此後仍保有自己的王表與外交看，答案是沒有的。可以確定的最後一點是，這場戰爭在亞述與巴比倫的關係上劃了一條分界：亞述證明了自己能把軍隊送過幼發拉底、平掉巴比倫的抵抗，並且能帶著神的象徵回家；巴比倫則證明了它可以被打劫而不滅亡，兩者此後一個多世紀維持著一種不平等的和平，直到前八世紀新亞述帝國把這層平衡徹底打破。
resultEn: The outcome divides into what is established and what is still argued. Established: the Assyrian army entered Babylon, took the spoil including the statue of Marduk, and carried the god back to Assur. The city was not razed, the Kassite rule was not interrupted, the king and his court remained in the city, and the Assyrians withdrew once they had their plunder. Still argued: first, whether this was a full siege or an Assyrian pressure that forced a submission by exploiting divisions inside the city; second, whether the god really remained at Assur for long or was sent back under the successor, a claim that later copies repeat but which, being late, cannot be treated as settled; third, whether Assyria afterwards held Babylon in actual client status, and from the fact that Babylon kept its own king list and its own foreign relations the answer appears to be no. The last thing that can be settled is this: the war drew a line in the relationship between the two countries. Assyria demonstrated that it could march an army across the Euphrates, break Babylonian resistance and bring home the symbol of a god; Babylon demonstrated that it could be plundered and survive, and for more than a century the two maintained an unequal peace, until the Neo-Assyrian empire of the eighth century BC broke the balance for good.
